fixes.explanation: Rich is a fair guess, friend. But verse 1 sends the good news to the poor. They are first on the speaker’s list (Isaiah 61:1). Nobody has to bring a big bank account to hear it.

Sending away would be a door closing. Isaiah 61:1 says something different: the speaker is sent to bind up the brokenhearted. Binding up is no door closing. The brokenhearted are bound up, not sent away.
True, and it’s the same sentence. The year of the LORD’s favor and the day of our God’s vengeance sit side by side in Isaiah 61:2. Two things proclaimed together.

Correct sounds close, and it even starts with the same letter. But nobody is getting corrected here. Verse 2 says the speaker is sent to comfort all who mourn (Isaiah 61:2). Comfort is the word for the mourners.

A crown of beauty, in place of ashes (Isaiah 61:3). Ashes are what’s left when the fire is done, and I’ve scraped enough burnt cookies off a tray to know it. A crown is something you put on your head on purpose. That is quite a swap.
Oaks of righteousness, friend. Verse 3 says the mourners will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD. Big, rooted and standing tall. Mourners called oaks, that’s quite a name.

Reeds by the water bend easy, so it’s a fair guess for something growing. But verse 3 says they will be called oaks of righteousness. They are the planting of the LORD. Reeds aren’t in this verse, oaks are.

True. Verse 6 begins with “But you will be called the priests of the LORD…” and goes on to say they will be spoken of as ministers of our God. The strangers handle flocks and fields in verse 5. God’s people are the ones called priests.
Burden is the opposite flavor, friend. Shame gets replaced, not doubled. Verse 7 says a double portion instead of shame.
False, you’ve got it. Verse 9 says their descendants will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples. These folks get noticed.
Blessed. Verse 9 says, “All who see them will acknowledge that they are a people the LORD has blessed.” People will see it with their own eyes. All who see them will say so.

A long life is a gift, but it isn’t the reason in this verse. The reason given is “for He has clothed me with garments of salvation…” (Isaiah 61:10). The text doesn’t mention years at all. It’s about the clothing.
